source_text: Omnta ergo recapitulans recapitulatus est, et adversus inimicum nostrum bellum provocans, et elidens eum qui, in initio in Adam captivos duxerat nos, et caleans ejus caput, quemadmodum habes in Genesi dixisse serpenti Deum: Et inimicitiam ponam inter te et inter mulierem, et inter semen tuum et semen ejus: tpse tuum lobservabit caput, et tu observabis ejus calcanewm, Ex eo enim qui ex muliere Virgine habebat nasci secundum similitudinem Adam, preeconabatur observans caput serpentis, id est semen, de quo ait Apostolus in epistola que est ad Galatas: Legem + factorum s positam, donec veniret semen cui promissum est. Manifestius autem adhue in eadem ostendit epistola, sic dicens: Cum autem venit plenitudo temporis, misit Deus Filium suum, factum de muliere. Neque enim juste victus fuisset inimicus, nisi ex muliere homo esset, qui vicit eum. Per mulierem enim homini dominatus est ab initio, semetipsum contrarium statuens homini. Propter hoc et Dominus semetipsum Filium Hominis confitetur, principalem hominem illum, ex quo ea que secundum mulierem est plasmatio facta est, in semetipsum recapitulans: uti quemadmodum per hominem victum descendit in mortem genus nostrum, sic iterum per victorem ascendamus in vitam. Et quemadmodum accepit palmam mors per hominem adversus nos, sic iterum nos adversus mortem per hominem accipiamus palmam. 2. Non autem Dominus antiquam illam et primam adversus serpentem inimicitiam in semetipso recapitulatus fuisset, adimplens promissionem Demiurgi, et perficiens preeceptum ejus, si ab alio venisset patre. Sed quoniam unus et idem est, qui ab initio plasmavit nos, et in fine Filium suum misit, preeceptum ejus perfecit Dominus, factus ex muliere, et destruens adversarium nostrum, et perficiens hominem secundum imaginem et similitudinem Et propter hoc non aliunde eum destruxit, nisi ex dictionibus Legis, et Patris preecepto adjutore usus ad destructionem et traductionem apostate angeli. Primo quidem diebus xu. jejunans, similiter ut Moyses et Helias, postea esuriit, ut hominem verum et firmum intelligamus: proprium enim est hominis, jejunantem esurire: deinde autem, ut haberet adversarius ubi congrederetur. Quoniam enim in principio per escam, non esurientem hominem seduxit transgredi preeceptum Dei, in fine esurientem non potuit dissuadere, eam que a Deo esset, sustinere escam. enim eo, et dicente: Si jilius Dei es, dic ut lapides isti panes fant; Dominus autem per preeceptum Legis repulit eum, dicens: Scriptum est, Non in pane tantum vivit homo. Ad illud quidem quod ait, Si filius Dei es, tacuit: exceecayit autem eum hominis confessione, et per paternam dictionem primum ejus impetum evacuavit. Que ergo fuit in Paradiso repletio hominis per duplicem gustationem, dissoluta est per eam, que fuit in hoe mundo, indigentiam. Ille autem legaliter explosus, tentabat et ipse per mandatum rursus legitime facere congressionem. In altissimum enim templi pinnaculum ducens eum, dixit: Si jilius Dei es, mitte te deorsum. Scriptum est enim: Quoniam Angelis swis Deus mandavit de te, et in manibus tollent te, ne forte offendas ad lapidem pedem twum, mendacium abscondens per Scripturam, quod Illud enim, quod Angelis suis mandavit de eo, scriptum erat; Mitte te autem deorsum, * de eo nulla dicebat sed a semetipso hane suasionem Diabolus afferebat. Dominus itaque legitime confutavit eum, dicens: Item seriptum in Lege ostendens id Yuidem quod est secundum hominem, quoniam non debet homo tentare Deum; quantum autem ad illum, in eo homine qui videbatur, non tentaret Dominum Deum suum. Elatio itaque sensus que fuit in serpente, dissoluta est per eam que fuit in homine humilitas: et bis jam victus erat de Scriptura Diabolus, cum est traductus, contraria preecepto Dei suadens, et secundum sententiam suam Dei hostis ostensus. Qui magne confutatus, et quasi semetipsum colligens, universam quam habebat virtutem in mendacium ordinans, tertio ostendit e seculi regna omnia, et gloriam ipsorum, dicens, quemadmodum meminit Lucas: Hee omnia tibi dabo, quoniam mihi tradita sunt, et cui volo do ea, si procidens adoraveris me. Dominus itaque eum qui esset: Vade, inquit, Satana; seriptum est Senim: Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, et illi soli servies. Denudans eum per hoe nomen, et se ostendens qui erat. Satana enim verbum Hebraicum, Apostatam significat. Et tertio itaque vincens eum, in reliquum repulit a semetipso quasi legitime vicet soluta est ea que fuerat in Adam preecepti Dei preevaricatio, per preeceptum legis, quod servavit Filius hominis non transgrediens preeceptum Dei. 8. Quis ergo Dominus Deus, cui Christus testimonium perhibet; quem nemo tentabit, et quem omnes adorare oportet, et soli servire? Omnimodo ille est sine dubio, qui et Legem dedit Deus. Heee enim in Lege preedicta fuerant, et per Legis sententiam ostendit Dominus, quoniam Lex quidem a Patre Verbum Domini annuntiat : apostata autem Dei angelus )per illius destruitur vocem, traductus Nquis esset, et victus a Filio hominis servante Dei preeceptum. Quoniam enim in initio homini suasit transgredi preceptum factoris, ideo eum habuit in sua potestate; potestas autem ejus est transgressio et apostasia, et his colligavit hominem ; per hominem ipsum iterum oportebat victum eum contrario colligari iisdem vinculis, quibus alligavit hominem, ut homo solutus revertatur ad suum Dominum, illa vincula relinquens, per }quze ipse fuerat alligatus, id est transgressionem. Illius enim colligatio, solutio facta est hominis, quoniam non potest ali> quis introire in domum fortis, et vasa ejus diripere, nisi primum ipsum fortem alligaverit. Contraria ergo in sermone ejus, qui omnia fecit Dei, traducens eum Dominus, et subjiciens per preeceptum, preeceptum autem Dei, lex; fugitivum eum Homo ejus et legis transgressorem, et apostatam Dei ostendens, postea jam ®Verbum constanter eum colligavit, quasi suum fugitivum, et diripuit ejus vasa, id est, eos qui ab eo detinebantur homines, quibus ipse injuste utebatur. Et captivus quidem ductus est juste is qui hominem injuste captivum duxerat; qui autem ante captivus ductus fuerat homo, extractus est a possessoris potestate, secundum misericordiam Dei Patris: qui miseratus est plasmati suo, et dedit salutem ei, per Verbum, id est per Christum redintegrans: ut experimento discat homo, quoniam non a semetipso, sed donatione Dei accipit incorruptelam. Dominus verus, et Deus unus a lege declaratur, et Evangelio per Christum ejus Filium manifestatur : quem solum adorare, et ab illo omnia bona exspectare oportet, non a Satana.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, recapitulating all things, He recapitulated, and provoking war against our enemy, and striking the one who, in the beginning, led us captive in Adam, and bruising his head, just as God said to the serpent in Genesis: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed: he will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel. For from the one who was to be born from the Virgin, according to the likeness of Adam, it was foretold that he would bruise the serpent's head, that is, the seed, about which the Apostle says in the epistle to the Galatians: The law of works was established until the seed to whom the promise was made should come. But more clearly, the same epistle shows, saying: But when the fullness of time came, God sent His Son, made from a woman. For the enemy would not have been justly conquered if a man from a woman had not conquered him. For through a woman, the enemy dominated man from the beginning, setting himself contrary to man. On account of this, the Lord also confesses Himself to be the Son of Man, the first man, from whom the creation that is according to the woman was made, recapitulating it in Himself: so that just as our race descended into death through the conquered man, so also we may ascend into life through the conqueror. And just as death received the palm against us through man, so also we will receive the palm against death through man. But the Lord would not have recapitulated in Himself the ancient and first enmity against the serpent, fulfilling the promise of the Creator and perfecting His command, if He had come from another father. But since He is one and the same who from the beginning created us and in the end sent His Son, the Lord perfected His command, made from a woman, and destroying our adversary, and perfecting man according to the image and likeness. And on account of this, He did not destroy him from anywhere else, except from the words of the Law and the command of the Father, using them as a helper for the destruction and translation of the apostate angel. First, indeed, on the fortieth day, fasting, similarly to Moses and Elijah, afterwards He hungered, so that we may understand Him to be a true and firm man: for it is proper to man to hunger when fasting: then, however, so that the adversary might have something to attack. For since in the beginning he deceived man, who was not hungry, to transgress the command of God through food, in the end he could not persuade the hungry one to sustain the food that was from God. For when he said: If you are the Son of God, say that these stones become bread, the Lord repelled him through the command of the Law, saying: It is written, Man does not live by bread alone. To that which he said, If you are the Son of God, He was silent: but He confounded him by the confession of man and through the paternal word, He first evacuated his attack. What, therefore, was the fullness of man in Paradise through the double tasting, was dissolved through the indigence that was in this world. But he, having been legally refuted, tried to make an attack again through the command. For leading Him to the highest pinnacle of the temple, he said: If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down. For it is written: For God has commanded His angels concerning you, and they will bear you in their hands, lest you strike your foot against a stone, hiding the lie through Scripture, that what was written concerning His angels, He said: Throw yourself down, however, he said nothing about Him, but the Devil was bringing this persuasion from himself. Therefore, the Lord legally confounded him, saying: It is also written in the Law, showing what is according to man, that man ought not to tempt God: as for Him, however, in the man who seemed to be, He did not tempt the Lord His God. The elevation of sense, therefore, which was in the serpent, was dissolved through the humility that was in man: and the Devil was already twice conquered from Scripture, when he was translated, persuading what was contrary to the command of God, and showing himself to be the enemy of God. Who, having been greatly confounded, and as if gathering himself, ordering all his power into a lie, showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, saying, as Luke remembers: I will give you all these things, because they have been handed over to me, and I give them to whomever I want, if you, falling down, will worship me. Therefore, the Lord said to him: Go, Satan; it is written: You will worship the Lord your God, and serve Him only. Uncovering him through this name, and showing Himself to be who He was. For Satan is a Hebrew word, signifying the apostate. And thus, conquering him for the third time, He repelled him from Himself, as if legally: the transgression of God's command, which was in Adam, was solved through the command of the Law, which the Son of Man kept, not transgressing the command of God. Who, therefore, is the Lord God, to whom Christ bears witness; whom no one will tempt, and whom all ought to adore, and serve only? Without a doubt, He is the one who gave the Law, God. For these things were predicted in the Law, and the Lord shows through the sentence of the Law, that the Law indeed announces the Word of the Lord from the Father: but the apostate angel of God is destroyed through His voice, translated, and conquered by the Son of Man, keeping the command of God. For since in the beginning he persuaded man to transgress the command of the Creator, therefore he had him in his power; but his power is transgression and apostasy, and through these he bound man: through man, however, it was necessary that he be conquered again, bound by the same chains by which he bound man, so that man, having been freed, may return to his Lord, leaving behind the chains by which he was bound, that is, transgression. For the binding of him was the liberation of man, since no one can enter the house of the strong and plunder his vessels, unless he first binds the strong one. Therefore, the Lord, translating him through the contrary in His word, and subjecting him through the command, and the command of God being the Law, showed him to be a fugitive from God and a transgressor of the Law, and an apostate of God: afterwards, indeed, the Word firmly bound him, as if he were His fugitive, and plundered his vessels, that is, the men who were detained by him, whom he was using unjustly. And the one who had led man captive unjustly was justly led captive: but the man who had been led captive before was extracted from the power of the possessor, according to the mercy of God the Father: who, having pitied His creation, gave salvation to him through the Word, that is, through Christ, restoring: so that man may learn by experience that he receives incorruptibility not from himself, but from the gift of God. The true Lord, and the one God, is declared by the Law, and is manifested through the Gospel by His Son, Christ: whom alone we ought to adore, and from whom we ought to expect all good things, not from Satan.

pass_b_english: He recapitulated all things by summing them up in Himself, declared war on our enemy, and struck down the one who first led us captive in Adam, crushing his head just as God told the serpent in Genesis: "I will put enmity between you and the woman, between your offspring and hers; he will crush your head, and you will strike his heel" (Gen 3:15). This offspring, foretold to be born of the Virgin in the likeness of Adam, is the "seed" Paul speaks of: "The law was added because of transgressions until the Seed to whom the promise referred should come" (Gal 3:19), and again, "When the fullness of time came, God sent His Son, born of a woman" (Gal 4:4). The enemy could not be justly conquered unless a man born of woman conquered him, since it was through a woman that he first gained dominion over man, setting himself against humanity. Therefore the Lord confesses Himself to be the Son of Man, the first Man from whom the formation according to woman originated, recapitulating that formation in Himself so that, just as our race descended into death through the conquered man, we might ascend into life through the Conqueror; just as death won the victory over us through a man, so we win the victory over death through a Man.

Had He come from another Father, the Lord could not have recapitulated in Himself that ancient primal enmity against the serpent, fulfilling the Creator's promise and perfecting His command. But because He is the very One who formed us at the beginning and sent His Son at the end, He fulfilled that command by being born of a woman, destroying our adversary, and restoring humanity to the image and likeness of God. He did not destroy the enemy by any other means than the words of the Law, using the Father's command as His instrument to overthrow and expose the apostate angel. After fasting forty days like Moses and Elijah, He became hungry — proving He was a true and steadfast man, since hunger is natural to a fasting human — and thus gave the adversary an opening to attack. In the beginning the devil deceived a man who was not hungry, luring him through food to break God's command; at the end he could not persuade the hungry One to turn aside from the food that comes from God. When he said, "If You are the Son of God, command these stones to become bread," the Lord drove him back with the Law's command: "It is written, 'Man shall not live by bread alone'" (Luke 4:4; Deut 8:3). To the taunt "If You are the Son of God," Jesus remained silent, but He confounded the tempter by confessing His humanity and answering with the Father's word, nullifying the first assault. The fullness humanity enjoyed in Paradise through a double tasting was undone by the deprivation endured in this world.

Legally repulsed, the devil tried again, misusing a command of Scripture. Taking Jesus to the temple's highest pinnacle, he said, "If You are the Son of God, throw Yourself down, for it is written, 'He will command His angels concerning You, and they will lift You up, lest You strike Your foot against a stone'" (Luke 4:10–11; Ps 91:11–12). He hid a lie inside Scripture: the promise was for the Messiah, not a command to leap. The Lord answered lawfully: "It is also written, 'You shall not put the Lord your God to the test'" (Luke 4:12; Deut 6:16), showing what befits a man — that a man must not tempt God — and that in the Man He appeared to be, He would not tempt the Lord His God. The serpent's pride was thus undone by human humility, and the devil was twice defeated by Scripture, exposed as God's enemy for urging what contradicted God's command. Stung, he gathered all his power into one great lie, showing Jesus all the kingdoms of the world and their glory: "All these I will give You, for they have been delivered to me, and I give them to whomever I will, if You will fall down and worship me" (Luke 4:6–7). The Lord commanded, "Be gone, Satan! For it is written, 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and Him only shall you serve'" (Luke 4:8; Deut 6:13). By that name — Satan, Hebrew for "the apostate" — He unmasked him, and with this third victory drove him away lawfully. The transgression of God's command that began in Adam was undone by the Law's command which the Son of Man kept without transgressing God's command.

Who then is the Lord God to whom Christ bears witness, whom no one may tempt, whom all must worship and serve alone? Without doubt He is the One who gave the Law — God Himself. These things were foretold in the Law, and by the Law's testimony the Lord demonstrates that the Law proclaims the Word of the Lord from the Father, while the apostate angel of God is destroyed by His voice, exposed and conquered by the Son of Man keeping God's command. Because the devil first persuaded man to break the Creator's command, he held man in his power; his power is transgression and apostasy, and by these he bound humanity. It was fitting that through a Man he should be conquered again, bound with the very chains he used to bind man, so that man, set free, might return to his Lord, leaving behind those chains — that is, transgression. The devil's binding became man's release, for no one can enter a strong man's house and plunder his goods unless he first binds the strong man (cf. Luke 11:21–22). Therefore the Lord, by the contrary word, exposed him as a fugitive from God, a transgressor of the Law, and an apostate, and subjected him by the command — for the command of God is the Law. Then the Word firmly bound him as His own runaway and plundered his goods: the men he had unjustly held captive. The one who unjustly led mankind captive was justly led captive; the man who had been captured was rescued from the possessor's power by the mercy of God the Father, who pitied His creation and gave it salvation through the Word — that is, through Christ — restoring it, so that humanity might learn by experience that incorruptibility comes not from itself but as God's gift. The true Lord and the one God is declared by the Law and revealed in the Gospel through His Son, Christ: Him alone we must worship, and from Him alone expect every good thing, not from Satan.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the theological nuances of the Latin text, particularly the concept of recapitulation and the legal/command-based nature of Christ's victory. Scripture citations in Pass B (Gen 3:15, Gal 3:19, Gal 4:4, Luke 4:4, Deut 8:3, Luke 4:10-11, Ps 91:11-12, Luke 4:12, Deut 6:16, Luke 4:6-7, Luke 4:8, Deut 6:13, Luke 11:21-22) correctly identify the biblical sources alluded to in the Latin, even where the Latin uses general references (e.g., 'in epistola que est ad Galatas' or 'Scriptum est'). Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Locked Latin.
